/-!
# Greenberg's conjectures

Two open conjectures of Ralph Greenberg in algebraic number theory.

* **Greenberg's invariants conjecture** (1971/1976). For every totally real number field $k$ and
  every prime $\ell$, the Iwasawa invariants of the cyclotomic $\mathbb{Z}_\ell$-extension
  $k_\infty/k$ vanish: $\lambda_\ell(k) = \mu_\ell(k) = 0$. Equivalently (by Iwasawa's formula
  $e_n = \lambda n + \mu \ell^n + \nu$ for $n \gg 0$), the exact power $\ell^{e_n}$ of $\ell$
  dividing the class number of the $n$-th layer $k_n$ of $k_\infty/k$ is bounded as
  $n \to \infty$. This bounded-class-number form is the one stated here.
* **Greenberg's $p$-rationality conjecture** (2016). For every odd prime $p$ and every $t$,
  there is a $p$-rational number field $K$ with
  $\operatorname{Gal}(K/\mathbb{Q}) \cong (\mathbb{Z}/2\mathbb{Z})^t$.

*References:*
* [Wikipedia, Greenberg's conjectures](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Greenberg%27s_conjectures)
* [Wikipedia, List of unsolved problems in mathematics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_unsolved_problems_in_mathematics)
* R. Greenberg, *On the Iwasawa invariants of totally real number fields*,
  Amer. J. Math. 98 (1976), 263–284.
* R. Greenberg, [*Galois representations with open image*](https://arxiv.org/abs/1408.6788),
  Ann. Math. Québec 40 (2016), 83–119, Conjecture 4.2.1.
* A. Movahhedi, T. Nguyen Quang Do, *Sur l'arithmétique des corps de nombres $p$-rationnels*,
  Séminaire de Théorie des Nombres, Paris 1987–88, Progr. Math. 81 (1990), 155–200.
-/

blocks.code:
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem greenbergs_conjectures.parts.i (k : Type*) [Field k] [NumberField k] [IsTotallyReal k]
    (ℓ : ℕ) [Fact ℓ.Prime] :
    ∃ C : ℕ, ∀ (n N : ℕ) (E : IntermediateField k (CyclotomicField (ℓ ^ N) k)),
      IsTotallyReal E → Module.finrank k E = ℓ ^ n → padicValNat ℓ (classNumber E) ≤ C := by
  sorry
blocks.docstring:
**Greenberg's invariants conjecture** (Greenberg, 1971/1976). Let $k$ be a totally real number
field and let $\ell$ be a prime. Let $k = k_0 \subset k_1 \subset k_2 \subset \cdots$ be the
layers of the cyclotomic $\mathbb{Z}_\ell$-extension $k_\infty/k$, so that $k_n/k$ is cyclic of
degree $\ell^n$. Then the Iwasawa invariants $\lambda_\ell(k)$ and $\mu_\ell(k)$ vanish;
equivalently (by Iwasawa's formula $e_n = \lambda n + \mu \ell^n + \nu$ for $n \gg 0$), the exact
power $\ell^{e_n}$ of $\ell$ dividing the class number of $k_n$ is bounded as $n \to \infty$.

Here $k_\infty$ is the unique $\mathbb{Z}_\ell$-extension of $k$ inside $k(\mu_{\ell^\infty})$
and $k_n$ is the unique subfield of $k_\infty$ with $[k_n : k] = \ell^n$. We do not construct
$k_\infty$ explicitly. Instead `E` ranges over the totally real intermediate fields of
$k(\mu_{\ell^N})/k$ of degree $\ell^n$ over $k$, for all $N$ and $n$; these are exactly the
layers $k_n$. Indeed, let $H = \operatorname{Gal}(k(\mu_{\ell^\infty})/k) \subseteq
\mathbb{Z}_\ell^\times$, so that $k_\infty$ is the fixed field of the torsion subgroup of $H$.
For odd $\ell$ this torsion has order dividing $\ell - 1$, so it fixes every subextension of
$\ell$-power degree; for $\ell = 2$ it is generated by $\zeta \mapsto \zeta^{-1}$, which is the
restriction of complex conjugation for every complex embedding (as $k$ is totally real), so it
fixes exactly the totally real subfields. In both cases such an $E$ lies in $k_\infty$ and hence
equals $k_n$; conversely each $k_n$ is a totally real subfield of some $k(\mu_{\ell^N})$ of
degree $\ell^n$ over $k$.

def IsUnramifiedOutside (p : ℕ) (K L : Type*) [Field K] [Field L] [Algebra K L] : Prop :=
  ∀ (P : Ideal (𝓞 L)) [P.IsPrime], P ≠ ⊥ → (p : 𝓞 L) ∉ P → Algebra.IsUnramifiedAt (𝓞 K) P
blocks.docstring:
A finite extension `L/K` of number fields is *unramified outside `p`* if every nonzero prime
ideal of `𝓞 L` not containing `p` (i.e. not lying above `p`) is unramified over `𝓞 K`. By
`Algebra.isUnramifiedAt_iff_of_isDedekindDomain` this says exactly that all such primes have
ramification index `1` over `𝓞 K`. Infinite places are not considered; for odd `p` a
`p`-extension is automatically unramified at the infinite places.

justification.closest_existing_considered: Algebra.IsUnramifiedAt (used pointwise), Ideal.ramificationIdx, NumberField.IsUnramifiedAtInfinitePlaces / InfinitePlace.IsUnramifiedIn (infinite places only), Algebra.unramifiedLocus.
justification.name: GreenbergsConjectures.IsUnramifiedOutside
justification.why_needed: Mathlib has Algebra.IsUnramifiedAt for a single prime but no predicate 'the finite extension F/K of number fields is unramified at every finite prime not above p', which is needed to describe p-ramified extensions.

blocks.name: IsUnramifiedOutside
blocks.text:
/--
A finite extension `L/K` of number fields is *unramified outside `p`* if every nonzero prime
ideal of `𝓞 L` not containing `p` (i.e. not lying above `p`) is unramified over `𝓞 K`. By
`Algebra.isUnramifiedAt_iff_of_isDedekindDomain` this says exactly that all such primes have
ramification index `1` over `𝓞 K`. Infinite places are not considered; for odd `p` a
`p`-extension is automatically unramified at the infinite places.
-/
def IsUnramifiedOutside (p : ℕ) (K L : Type*) [Field K] [Field L] [Algebra K L] : Prop :=
  ∀ (P : Ideal (𝓞 L)) [P.IsPrime], P ≠ ⊥ → (p : 𝓞 L) ∉ P → Algebra.IsUnramifiedAt (𝓞 K) P

noncomputable def maxAbelianPExtension (p : ℕ) (K : Type*) [Field K] :
    IntermediateField K (AlgebraicClosure K) :=
  ⨆ L ∈ {L : IntermediateField K (AlgebraicClosure K) | FiniteDimensional K L ∧ IsGalois K L ∧
    IsMulCommutative (L ≃ₐ[K] L) ∧ IsPGroup p (L ≃ₐ[K] L) ∧ IsUnramifiedOutside p K L}, L
blocks.docstring:
The maximal abelian pro-`p` extension of `K` unramified outside `p`, as a subfield of a fixed
algebraic closure of `K`: the compositum of all finite abelian extensions `L/K` of `p`-power
degree that are unramified outside `p`.

justification.closest_existing_considered: IntermediateField.iSup / ⨆ over intermediate fields of AlgebraicClosure K (used), Field.absoluteGaloisGroup, IsCyclotomicExtension (not applicable).
justification.name: GreenbergsConjectures.maxAbelianPExtension
justification.why_needed: The maximal abelian pro-p extension of a number field unramified outside p (compositum of all finite abelian p-power-degree extensions unramified outside p) does not exist in Mathlib; needed to define p-rationality.

@[category API, AMS 11]
theorem le_maxAbelianPExtension (p : ℕ) (K : Type*) [Field K]
    (L : IntermediateField K (AlgebraicClosure K)) [FiniteDimensional K L] [IsGalois K L]
    [IsMulCommutative (L ≃ₐ[K] L)] (hL : IsPGroup p (L ≃ₐ[K] L))
    (hL' : IsUnramifiedOutside p K L) : L ≤ maxAbelianPExtension p K :=
  le_iSup₂_of_le L ⟨‹_›, ‹_›, ‹_›, hL, hL'⟩ le_rfl
blocks.docstring:

contained in `maxAbelianPExtension p K`.

@[category API, AMS 11]
theorem le_maxAbelianPExtension (p : ℕ) (K : Type*) [Field K]
    (L : IntermediateField K (AlgebraicClosure K)) [FiniteDimensional K L] [IsGalois K L]
    [IsMulCommutative (L ≃ₐ[K] L)] (hL : IsPGroup p (L ≃ₐ[K] L))
    (hL' : IsUnramifiedOutside p K L) : L ≤ maxAbelianPExtension p K :=
  le_iSup₂_of_le L ⟨‹_›, ‹_›, ‹_›, hL, hL'⟩ le_rfl

blocks.docstring:
A number field `K` is *`p`-rational* if the Galois group of its maximal abelian pro-`p`
extension unramified outside `p` is isomorphic, as a topological group (Krull topology), to
$\mathbb{Z}_p^{r_2 + 1}$, where $r_2$ is the number of complex places of `K`.

This is the form of the definition used by Greenberg (2016). For odd `p` it is equivalent
(Movahhedi–Nguyen Quang Do) to the original definition: the Galois group of the maximal pro-`p`
extension of `K` unramified outside `p` is a free pro-`p` group. Since this Galois group is
$\mathbb{Z}_p^{r_2 + 1 + \delta} \oplus T$ with $\delta$ the Leopoldt defect and $T$ finite,
it is also equivalent to: Leopoldt's conjecture holds for `K` at `p` and $T$ is trivial.
The definition is only intended for odd `p`; for `p = 2` conventions about the infinite places
differ in the literature.

justification.closest_existing_considered: No pro-p / free pro-p group notion in Mathlib; ContinuousMulEquiv, krullTopology, PadicInt and nrComplexPlaces are reused.
justification.name: GreenbergsConjectures.IsPRational
justification.why_needed: p-rationality of a number field is not in Mathlib or FormalConjecturesForMathlib; defined as Gal(M/K) ≃ₜ* Multiplicative (Fin (nrComplexPlaces K + 1) → ℤ_[p]) with the Krull topology (equivalent to the free-pro-p definition for odd p).

blocks.name: IsPRational
blocks.text:
/--
A number field `K` is *`p`-rational* if the Galois group of its maximal abelian pro-`p`
extension unramified outside `p` is isomorphic, as a topological group (Krull topology), to
$\mathbb{Z}_p^{r_2 + 1}$, where $r_2$ is the number of complex places of `K`.

This is the form of the definition used by Greenberg (2016). For odd `p` it is equivalent
(Movahhedi–Nguyen Quang Do) to the original definition: the Galois group of the maximal pro-`p`
extension of `K` unramified outside `p` is a free pro-`p` group. Since this Galois group is
$\mathbb{Z}_p^{r_2 + 1 + \delta} \oplus T$ with $\delta$ the Leopoldt defect and $T$ finite,
it is also equivalent to: Leopoldt's conjecture holds for `K` at `p` and $T$ is trivial.
The definition is only intended for odd `p`; for `p = 2` conventions about the infinite places
differ in the literature.
-/
def IsPRational (p : ℕ) [Fact p.Prime] (K : Type*) [Field K] [NumberField K] : Prop :=
  Nonempty ((maxAbelianPExtension p K ≃ₐ[K] maxAbelianPExtension p K) ≃ₜ*
    Multiplicative (Fin (nrComplexPlaces K + 1) → ℤ_[p]))

blocks.code:
@[category test, AMS 11]
theorem isPRational_rat (p : ℕ) [Fact p.Prime] (hp : Odd p) : IsPRational p ℚ := by
  sorry
blocks.docstring:
Sanity check for the definition: $\mathbb{Q}$ is $p$-rational for every odd prime $p$. By the
Kronecker–Weber theorem, the maximal abelian pro-$p$ extension of $\mathbb{Q}$ unramified outside
$p$ is the cyclotomic $\mathbb{Z}_p$-extension, whose Galois group is
$\mathbb{Z}_p = \mathbb{Z}_p^{0 + 1}$.

theorem greenbergs_conjectures.parts.ii (p : ℕ) [Fact p.Prime] (hp : Odd p) (t : ℕ) :
    ∃ (K : Type) (_ : Field K) (_ : NumberField K), IsGalois ℚ K ∧
      Nonempty ((K ≃ₐ[ℚ] K) ≃* Multiplicative (Fin t → ZMod 2)) ∧ IsPRational p K := by
  sorry
blocks.docstring:
**Greenberg's $p$-rationality conjecture** (Greenberg, 2016, Conjecture 4.2.1). For every odd
prime $p$ and every $t$, there exists a $p$-rational number field $K$, Galois over $\mathbb{Q}$,
with $\operatorname{Gal}(K/\mathbb{Q}) \cong (\mathbb{Z}/2\mathbb{Z})^t$.

The case $t = 0$ is included; it holds with $K = \mathbb{Q}$.

claims.decomposer_note: Greenberg's invariants conjecture (1971/1976): for every totally real number field k and every prime ℓ, the Iwasawa invariants λ and μ of the cyclotomic Z_ℓ-extension k_∞/k vanish, which (by Iwasawa's formula e_n = λn + μℓ^n + ν) is equivalent to the article's 1976 form that the exact power of ℓ dividing the class number of the n-th layer k_n (the unique subfield of k(μ_{ℓ^∞}) cyclic of degree ℓ^n over k) stays bounded as n → ∞ — the bounded-class-number form is the tractable one to formalize since Iwasawa invariants are not in Mathlib; the cyclotomic Z_ℓ-extension exists for every k so no Leopoldt hypothesis is needed, and the article's 'related conjecture' μ_ℓ(k)=0 for arbitrary k (Iwasawa's μ=0 conjecture, with the solved Ferrero–Washington abelian case) is not one of Greenberg's conjectures and is deliberately omitted.
claims.reviewer_why: All seven formalizations of this slot are mathematically faithful (bounded ℓ-adic valuation of class numbers of the layers of the cyclotomic Z_ℓ-extension; I verified the layer characterizations, including ℓ = 2, where 'totally real' is exactly the condition of being fixed by −1 ∈ Gal(k(μ_{2^∞})/k), and the tower-uniqueness argument of c01/c08). c04's statement is the simplest and uses only Mathlib primitives: E ranges over totally real intermediate fields of k(μ_{ℓ^N})/k of degree ℓ^n over k, which are exactly the layers k_n for every prime ℓ; classNumber is used directly (c08 needed Nat.card (ClassGroup _), c01/c06 needed redundant instance binders, c02/c03/c07 needed a bespoke layer predicate and quantification over Types). Docstring lightly edited to spell out the ℓ = 2 argument.
claims.source_text: Simply speaking, the conjecture asks whether we have $\mu _{\ell }(k)=\lambda _{\ell }(k)=0$ for any totally real number field $k$ and any prime number $\ell$
claims.text_span: Simply speaking, the conjecture asks whether we have {\displaystyle \mu _{\ell }(k)=\lambda _{\ell }(k)=0} for any totally real number field {\displaystyle k} and any prime number {\displaystyle \ell }

claims.decomposer_note: Greenberg's generalized (pseudo-null) conjecture, 2001, subordinate to part i as its generalization: with F̃ the compositum of all Z_p-extensions of F, Gal(F̃/F) ≅ Z_p^n, L̃ the maximal unramified abelian pro-p extension (pro-p Hilbert class field) of F̃, X̃ = Gal(L̃/F̃) is pseudo-null over Λ̃ = Z_p[[Gal(F̃/F)]] ≅ Z_p[[T_1,…,T_n]] (i.e. its annihilator has height ≥ 2, equivalently for n = 1 X̃ is finite); the article states it for totally real F but Greenberg's 2001 source (and the article's own 'possible reformulation' with k̃) states it for an arbitrary number field F, and only the arbitrary-field version genuinely generalizes part i (for totally real F under Leopoldt it reduces to λ = μ = 0), so the arbitrary-F form should be stated with the discrepancy documented.
claims.reviewer_why: Omitted by all 8 candidates, and I agree: a faithful statement needs the compositum F̃ of all Z_p-extensions, the maximal unramified abelian pro-p extension of the infinite field F̃ (Mathlib's Algebra.IsUnramifiedAt is only meaningful in the finite/Dedekind setting), the Iwasawa algebra Z_p[[Gal(F̃/F)]] with its continuous action on the profinite group X̃, and pseudo-nullity; none exist in Mathlib or FormalConjecturesForMathlib, and there is no layer-wise elementary reformulation for Z_p^n-extensions with n ≥ 2. Building this bespoke would be a large unverifiable construction; the risk of an unfaithful statement is too high.

claims.decomposer_note: Greenberg's p-rationality conjecture (Greenberg 2016, 'Galois representations with open image', Conj. 4.2.1): for every odd prime p and every integer t ≥ 1 there is a number field K, Galois over ℚ with Gal(K/ℚ) ≅ (ℤ/2ℤ)^t (a multiquadratic field), that is p-rational, meaning the Galois group of the maximal pro-p extension of K unramified outside p is a free pro-p group (equivalently, K satisfies Leopoldt's conjecture at p and the torsion of the Galois group of the maximal abelian pro-p extension unramified outside p is trivial); p-rationality is not in Mathlib and must be defined, and t = 0 is trivially satisfied by K = ℚ so allowing t = 0 is harmless but the quantifier is really over t ≥ 1.
claims.reviewer_why: c04, c05, c06 and c08 give essentially the same faithful definition: K is p-rational iff Gal(M/K) ≅ Z_p^{r_2+1} (Krull topology), M = compositum in an algebraic closure of all finite abelian p-power-degree extensions unramified (Algebra.IsUnramifiedAt, equivalent to e = 1 by Algebra.isUnramifiedAt_iff_of_isDedekindDomain) at all finite primes not above p. For odd p this is equivalent to the free-pro-p definition (Movahhedi–Nguyen Quang Do; Euler characteristic χ(G_S(p)) = −r_2), and it is exactly 'Leopoldt at p and trivial torsion', the form accepted by the decomposition notes. c08 chosen because its bespoke definitions need no NumberField instance juggling and come with two proved API lemmas; c04's sorry'd sanity test 'ℚ is p-rational for odd p' was added (category test). Conjecture: ∀ odd prime p, ∀ t : ℕ, ∃ number field K, IsGalois ℚ K ∧ Gal(K/ℚ) ≃* (Z/2)^t ∧ IsPRational p K (t = 0 harmless, per notes). The omission reasons of c01/c02/c03/c07 (no free pro-p groups) are not convincing since the equivalent abelian formulation avoids them.

context: Greenberg's conjecture is either of two conjectures in algebraic number theory proposed by Ralph Greenberg. Both are still unsolved as of 2021.

decomposition_objections.text: Minor: the notes for parts.i describe k_n as 'the unique subfield of k(μ_{ℓ^∞}) cyclic of degree ℓ^n over k'. This is inaccurate for ℓ = 2: for totally real k, Gal(k(μ_{2^∞})/k) contains the torsion element −1 and k(μ_{2^∞}) has three cyclic subextensions of degree 2^n over k (e.g. for k = ℚ: ℚ(μ_{2^{n+1}}), ℚ(μ_{2^{n+2}})^+, ℚ(ζ−ζ^{-1})); only the totally real one is the layer of the cyclotomic Z_2-extension. The file therefore characterises the layers as the totally real intermediate fields of k(μ_{ℓ^N}) of degree ℓ^n over k, which is correct for all primes ℓ. Also, the pseudo_null slot is not formalizable with current primitives (see per_slot).

The note for parts.i describes k_n as 'the unique subfield of k(μ_{ℓ^∞}) cyclic of degree ℓ^n over k'. This is false for ℓ = 2: for totally real k, Gal(k(μ_{2^∞})/k) ≅ ℤ/2 × ℤ_2, so e.g. for k = ℚ the fields ℚ(i), ℚ(√2), ℚ(√-2) are all cyclic of degree 2 inside ℚ(μ_{2^∞}), and only ℚ(√2) is the first layer of the cyclotomic ℤ_2-extension. Uniqueness holds only for odd ℓ, or once one asks for the whole nested tower (or for totally real layers). The formalization therefore quantifies over the full tower k_0 ⊆ k_1 ⊆ … with cyclic layers of degree ℓ^n inside k(μ_{ℓ^∞}), which pins down the cyclotomic ℤ_ℓ-extension for every prime ℓ. Otherwise the table is fine; the pseudo-null slot cannot be stated with existing primitives (see per-slot).

import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Greenberg's conjectures

Two open conjectures of Ralph Greenberg in algebraic number theory.

* **Greenberg's invariants conjecture** (1971/1976). For every totally real number field $k$ and
  every prime $\ell$, the Iwasawa invariants of the cyclotomic $\mathbb{Z}_\ell$-extension
  $k_\infty/k$ vanish: $\lambda_\ell(k) = \mu_\ell(k) = 0$. Equivalently (by Iwasawa's formula
  $e_n = \lambda n + \mu \ell^n + \nu$ for $n \gg 0$), the exact power $\ell^{e_n}$ of $\ell$
  dividing the class number of the $n$-th layer $k_n$ of $k_\infty/k$ is bounded as
  $n \to \infty$. This bounded-class-number form is the one stated here.
* **Greenberg's $p$-rationality conjecture** (2016). For every odd prime $p$ and every $t$,
  there is a $p$-rational number field $K$ with
  $\operatorname{Gal}(K/\mathbb{Q}) \cong (\mathbb{Z}/2\mathbb{Z})^t$.

*References:*
* [Wikipedia, Greenberg's conjectures](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Greenberg%27s_conjectures)
* [Wikipedia, List of unsolved problems in mathematics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_unsolved_problems_in_mathematics)
* R. Greenberg, *On the Iwasawa invariants of totally real number fields*,
  Amer. J. Math. 98 (1976), 263–284.
* R. Greenberg, [*Galois representations with open image*](https://arxiv.org/abs/1408.6788),
  Ann. Math. Québec 40 (2016), 83–119, Conjecture 4.2.1.
* A. Movahhedi, T. Nguyen Quang Do, *Sur l'arithmétique des corps de nombres $p$-rationnels*,
  Séminaire de Théorie des Nombres, Paris 1987–88, Progr. Math. 81 (1990), 155–200.
-/

open NumberField NumberField.InfinitePlace

namespace GreenbergsConjectures

/--
**Greenberg's invariants conjecture** (Greenberg, 1971/1976). Let $k$ be a totally real number
field and let $\ell$ be a prime. Let $k = k_0 \subset k_1 \subset k_2 \subset \cdots$ be the
layers of the cyclotomic $\mathbb{Z}_\ell$-extension $k_\infty/k$, so that $k_n/k$ is cyclic of
degree $\ell^n$. Then the Iwasawa invariants $\lambda_\ell(k)$ and $\mu_\ell(k)$ vanish;
equivalently (by Iwasawa's formula $e_n = \lambda n + \mu \ell^n + \nu$ for $n \gg 0$), the exact
power $\ell^{e_n}$ of $\ell$ dividing the class number of $k_n$ is bounded as $n \to \infty$.

Here $k_\infty$ is the unique $\mathbb{Z}_\ell$-extension of $k$ inside $k(\mu_{\ell^\infty})$
and $k_n$ is the unique subfield of $k_\infty$ with $[k_n : k] = \ell^n$. We do not construct
$k_\infty$ explicitly. Instead `E` ranges over the totally real intermediate fields of
$k(\mu_{\ell^N})/k$ of degree $\ell^n$ over $k$, for all $N$ and $n$; these are exactly the
layers $k_n$. Indeed, let $H = \operatorname{Gal}(k(\mu_{\ell^\infty})/k) \subseteq
\mathbb{Z}_\ell^\times$, so that $k_\infty$ is the fixed field of the torsion subgroup of $H$.
For odd $\ell$ this torsion has order dividing $\ell - 1$, so it fixes every subextension of
$\ell$-power degree; for $\ell = 2$ it is generated by $\zeta \mapsto \zeta^{-1}$, which is the
restriction of complex conjugation for every complex embedding (as $k$ is totally real), so it
fixes exactly the totally real subfields. In both cases such an $E$ lies in $k_\infty$ and hence
equals $k_n$; conversely each $k_n$ is a totally real subfield of some $k(\mu_{\ell^N})$ of
degree $\ell^n$ over $k$.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem greenbergs_conjectures.parts.i (k : Type*) [Field k] [NumberField k] [IsTotallyReal k]
    (ℓ : ℕ) [Fact ℓ.Prime] :
    ∃ C : ℕ, ∀ (n N : ℕ) (E : IntermediateField k (CyclotomicField (ℓ ^ N) k)),
      IsTotallyReal E → Module.finrank k E = ℓ ^ n → padicValNat ℓ (classNumber E) ≤ C := by
  sorry

/--
A finite extension `L/K` of number fields is *unramified outside `p`* if every nonzero prime
ideal of `𝓞 L` not containing `p` (i.e. not lying above `p`) is unramified over `𝓞 K`. By
`Algebra.isUnramifiedAt_iff_of_isDedekindDomain` this says exactly that all such primes have
ramification index `1` over `𝓞 K`. Infinite places are not considered; for odd `p` a
`p`-extension is automatically unramified at the infinite places.
-/
def IsUnramifiedOutside (p : ℕ) (K L : Type*) [Field K] [Field L] [Algebra K L] : Prop :=
  ∀ (P : Ideal (𝓞 L)) [P.IsPrime], P ≠ ⊥ → (p : 𝓞 L) ∉ P → Algebra.IsUnramifiedAt (𝓞 K) P

/--
The maximal abelian pro-`p` extension of `K` unramified outside `p`, as a subfield of a fixed
algebraic closure of `K`: the compositum of all finite abelian extensions `L/K` of `p`-power
degree that are unramified outside `p`.
-/
noncomputable def maxAbelianPExtension (p : ℕ) (K : Type*) [Field K] :
    IntermediateField K (AlgebraicClosure K) :=
  ⨆ L ∈ {L : IntermediateField K (AlgebraicClosure K) | FiniteDimensional K L ∧ IsGalois K L ∧
    IsMulCommutative (L ≃ₐ[K] L) ∧ IsPGroup p (L ≃ₐ[K] L) ∧ IsUnramifiedOutside p K L}, L

/-- The trivial extension `K/K` is unramified outside any `p`. -/
@[category API, AMS 11]
theorem isUnramifiedOutside_self (p : ℕ) (K : Type*) [Field K] : IsUnramifiedOutside p K K :=
  fun _ _ _ _ ↦ inferInstance

/-- Every finite abelian extension of `K` of `p`-power degree that is unramified outside `p` is
contained in `maxAbelianPExtension p K`. -/
@[category API, AMS 11]
theorem le_maxAbelianPExtension (p : ℕ) (K : Type*) [Field K]
    (L : IntermediateField K (AlgebraicClosure K)) [FiniteDimensional K L] [IsGalois K L]
    [IsMulCommutative (L ≃ₐ[K] L)] (hL : IsPGroup p (L ≃ₐ[K] L))
    (hL' : IsUnramifiedOutside p K L) : L ≤ maxAbelianPExtension p K :=
  le_iSup₂_of_le L ⟨‹_›, ‹_›, ‹_›, hL, hL'⟩ le_rfl

/--
A number field `K` is *`p`-rational* if the Galois group of its maximal abelian pro-`p`
extension unramified outside `p` is isomorphic, as a topological group (Krull topology), to
$\mathbb{Z}_p^{r_2 + 1}$, where $r_2$ is the number of complex places of `K`.

This is the form of the definition used by Greenberg (2016). For odd `p` it is equivalent
(Movahhedi–Nguyen Quang Do) to the original definition: the Galois group of the maximal pro-`p`
extension of `K` unramified outside `p` is a free pro-`p` group. Since this Galois group is
$\mathbb{Z}_p^{r_2 + 1 + \delta} \oplus T$ with $\delta$ the Leopoldt defect and $T$ finite,
it is also equivalent to: Leopoldt's conjecture holds for `K` at `p` and $T$ is trivial.
The definition is only intended for odd `p`; for `p = 2` conventions about the infinite places
differ in the literature.
-/
def IsPRational (p : ℕ) [Fact p.Prime] (K : Type*) [Field K] [NumberField K] : Prop :=
  Nonempty ((maxAbelianPExtension p K ≃ₐ[K] maxAbelianPExtension p K) ≃ₜ*
    Multiplicative (Fin (nrComplexPlaces K + 1) → ℤ_[p]))

/--
Sanity check for the definition: $\mathbb{Q}$ is $p$-rational for every odd prime $p$. By the
Kronecker–Weber theorem, the maximal abelian pro-$p$ extension of $\mathbb{Q}$ unramified outside
$p$ is the cyclotomic $\mathbb{Z}_p$-extension, whose Galois group is
$\mathbb{Z}_p = \mathbb{Z}_p^{0 + 1}$.
-/
@[category test, AMS 11]
theorem isPRational_rat (p : ℕ) [Fact p.Prime] (hp : Odd p) : IsPRational p ℚ := by
  sorry

/--
**Greenberg's $p$-rationality conjecture** (Greenberg, 2016, Conjecture 4.2.1). For every odd
prime $p$ and every $t$, there exists a $p$-rational number field $K$, Galois over $\mathbb{Q}$,
with $\operatorname{Gal}(K/\mathbb{Q}) \cong (\mathbb{Z}/2\mathbb{Z})^t$.

The case $t = 0$ is included; it holds with $K = \mathbb{Q}$.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem greenbergs_conjectures.parts.ii (p : ℕ) [Fact p.Prime] (hp : Odd p) (t : ℕ) :
    ∃ (K : Type) (_ : Field K) (_ : NumberField K), IsGalois ℚ K ∧
      Nonempty ((K ≃ₐ[ℚ] K) ≃* Multiplicative (Fin t → ZMod 2)) ∧ IsPRational p K := by
  sorry

end GreenbergsConjectures

items: parts.i: the conjecture is stated positively (as a conjecture, 'λ=μ=0 holds'), not with answer(sorry), although the 1976 text phrases it as a question; the Wikipedia article and the notes treat it as Greenberg's conjecture.

parts.i: λ_ℓ(K)=μ_ℓ(K)=0 is encoded as boundedness of the exact power of ℓ dividing the class numbers of the layers (equivalent via Iwasawa's theorem e_n = λn + μℓ^n + ν), as recommended by the notes since Iwasawa invariants are not in Mathlib.

parts.i: the layers K_n of the cyclotomic Z_ℓ-extension are not constructed; instead E ranges over all totally real intermediate fields of CyclotomicField (ℓ^N) K over K with finrank K E = ℓ^n, for all N and n. Reviewer should check the claim (in the docstring) that these are exactly the K_n: for odd ℓ the torsion of Gal(K(μ_{ℓ^∞})/K) ⊆ Z_ℓ^× has order dividing ℓ−1 so fixes any ℓ-power-degree subextension; for ℓ=2 it is {±1} and the totally real condition forces fixedness under −1 (complex conjugation). Conversely each K_n is totally real and lies in some K(μ_{ℓ^N}).
parts.i: the prime is taken as (ℓ : ℕ) [Fact ℓ.Prime]; the ℓ-adic valuation of the class number is padicValNat ℓ (classNumber E).

parts.ii: p-rationality is defined by the equivalent condition Gal(M/K) ≅ Z_p^{r_2+1} (topological group iso, Krull topology), where M is the maximal abelian pro-p extension of K unramified outside p, instead of the original 'maximal pro-p extension unramified outside p has free pro-p Galois group' (free pro-p groups are not in Mathlib). For odd p this equivalence is a theorem of Movahhedi–Nguyen Quang Do (Gal(M/K) ≅ Z_p^{r_2+1+δ} ⊕ T with δ the Leopoldt defect; free pro-p ⟺ δ=0 ∧ T=0). The definition is only asserted to agree with the standard one for odd p, which is the only case used.

parts.ii: 'unramified outside p' is taken at finite primes only: every nonzero prime P of 𝓞 F with p ∉ P satisfies Algebra.IsUnramifiedAt (𝓞 K) P (equivalently ramification index 1, by Algebra.isUnramifiedAt_iff_of_isDedekindDomain). Infinite places are ignored, which is harmless for odd p.

parts.ii: M is realised concretely as the sSup (compositum) inside AlgebraicClosure K of all finite intermediate fields F with IsGalois K F, abelian Galois group (IsMulCommutative), IsPGroup p (F ≃ₐ[K] F) and unramified outside p; the NumberField instance on such F is obtained via NumberField.of_module_finite.

parts.ii: Gal(K/ℚ) ≅ (Z/2Z)^t is encoded as Nonempty ((K ≃ₐ[ℚ] K) ≃* Multiplicative (Fin t → ZMod 2)) together with IsGalois ℚ K; K is an existentially quantified Type with Field and NumberField instances (repo idiom, cf. WallSunSun.lean).
parts.ii: t ranges over all of ℕ (the article says 'for any t'); t = 0 is the harmless true case K = ℚ. The prime is (p : ℕ) [Fact p.Prime] (hp : Odd p).

An extra @[category test] statement isPRational_rat (ℚ is p-rational for odd p, with sorry) is included as a sanity check of the bespoke definition, following the CONTRIBUTING request for basic API tests of bespoke definitions.

parts.i: the layers of the cyclotomic ℤ_ℓ-extension are characterised, not constructed: the theorem is universally quantified over towers K : ℕ → IntermediateField k (AlgebraicClosure k) with K n ≤ k(μ_{ℓ^∞}), Monotone K, IsGalois k (K n), IsCyclic Gal(K n/k), finrank k (K n) = ℓ^n. Reviewer should check the argument that such a tower exists and is unique (union is a ℤ_ℓ-extension inside k(μ_{ℓ^∞}); Gal(k(μ_{ℓ^∞})/k) ≅ (finite)×ℤ_ℓ has a unique ℤ_ℓ-quotient; layers of a ℤ_ℓ-extension are unique). Existence makes the statement non-vacuous.

parts.i: class number written as Nat.card (ClassGroup (𝓞 (K n))) rather than NumberField.classNumber, to avoid needing a NumberField instance on K n (which follows from hdeg but is not available to instance search). Since K n is finite over k the class group is finite and Nat.card equals the class number; the '0 for infinite types' default is unreachable.
parts.i: k(μ_{ℓ^∞}) is IntermediateField.adjoin k {ζ | ∃ m, ζ ^ ℓ ^ m = 1} inside AlgebraicClosure k. 'Power of ℓ dividing h(k_n) is bounded' is ∃ B, ∀ n, padicValNat ℓ h_n ≤ B.

parts.ii: p-rationality is defined by Gal(K^{ab}_{p}/K) ≃ₜ* ℤ_p^{r₂+1} (Krull topology; Multiplicative (Fin (nrComplexPlaces K + 1) → ℤ_[p])), the standard equivalent of Greenberg's 'free pro-p' definition for odd p (Movahhedi–Nguyen Quang Do; Euler characteristic argument h²(G_S(p),ℤ/p) = δ_Leopoldt + d(T)). Free pro-p groups are not in Mathlib; the abelian form combines 'Leopoldt at p' (ℤ_p-rank r₂+1) and 'torsion trivial' in one condition. The definition is only claimed correct for odd p; the conjecture has hypothesis Odd p.

parts.ii: 'unramified outside p' for a finite extension L/K uses Mathlib's Algebra.IsUnramifiedAt (𝓞 K) P for nonzero primes P of 𝓞 L with p ∉ P (equivalent to e(P)=1 by Algebra.isUnramifiedAt_iff_of_isDedekindDomain). Infinite places are not mentioned, which is harmless for odd p. The maximal abelian pro-p extension unramified outside p is the compositum (iSup) of all finite-dimensional Galois L ⊆ AlgebraicClosure K with IsMulCommutative and IsPGroup p Galois group and IsUnramifiedOutside p K L; the FiniteDimensional restriction keeps Mathlib's unramified notion in its classical Dedekind setting.

parts.ii: t ranges over all of ℕ (the article says 'for any t'); t = 0 is the known p-rationality of ℚ, so this does not change the truth value versus t ≥ 1. The existential field K lives in Type, following WallSunSun.lean.
Gal(K/ℚ) ≅ (ℤ/2ℤ)^t is Nonempty ((K ≃ₐ[ℚ] K) ≃* Multiplicative (Fin t → ZMod 2)), with IsGalois ℚ K assumed (via the canonical ℚ-algebra structure on a char-0 field).

Two @[category API] lemmas (trivial extension is unramified outside p; every qualifying finite extension lies in maxAbelianPExtension) are included as basic tests of the bespoke definitions, both proved.

reviewer_notes: Final file states parts.i (invariants conjecture, bounded-class-number form) and parts.ii (p-rationality conjecture) and omits variants.pseudo_null. Compiles with only 'declaration uses sorry' warnings (3: the two conjectures and the sanity test isPRational_rat). Ambiguities: (1) the Wikipedia article states the pseudo-null conjecture for totally real F while Greenberg 2001 states it for arbitrary F — moot since the slot is omitted for missing primitives (Iwasawa algebra, pseudo-null modules, unramifiedness over infinite extensions). (2) The decomposition note that k_n is 'the unique subfield of k(μ_{ℓ^∞}) cyclic of degree ℓ^n over k' is wrong for ℓ = 2 (e.g. ℚ(i), ℚ(√2), ℚ(√−2)); the final statement handles this via the totally-real condition, which for ℓ = 2 is exactly membership in the cyclotomic Z_2-extension, and is automatic for odd ℓ. (3) p-rationality is defined by the abelian criterion Gal(M/K) ≅ Z_p^{r_2+1} rather than 'free pro-p'; these are equivalent for odd p (the only case in the conjecture) and the docstring says so. Infinite places are ignored in 'unramified outside p', harmless for odd p. Quantifier t ranges over all ℕ (article: 'for any t'); t = 0 holds with K = ℚ.
title: Greenberg's conjectures
